title: Team USA bounces back from rough outing by dominating Czechia
content:
After a nail-biting win over Italy, Team USA responded convincingly in its final World Cup group stage game a day later, defeating Czechia 105-64. The victory Monday in Berlin clinched first place in Group D for the Americans, allowing them to bypass the qualification for the quarterfinals. They await the winner of Hungary versus Japan in the final eight Thursday.

Team USA’s offense was much cleaner than it was in a 55-52 win against Italy. The four-time defending World Cup champs exceeded their total score from Sunday with 57 first-half points against Czechia, and they finished the game shooting 52 percent from the field. Against the Czech defense that suffocated the paint and sprinkled in occasional zone defense, the 3-ball opened things for the Americans. Breanna Stewart hit their first triple within the first minute, and Team USA had seven on the day.

Stewart set the tone in many ways in the first quarter. She rebounded from a rough shooting outing in the second group stage contest by hitting 8 of 11 field goals and scoring 19 points. She also posted six assists with zero turnovers and spearheaded the Americans’ transition offense with her rim-running.

“I wanted to come out and really lead this team in a number of ways,” Stewart said on the broadcast postgame. “Wanted to make sure that today we really took things into our own hands and really lead by example.”

Team USA’s off-ball movement was significantly improved against the zone, particularly with the perimeter crew of Paige Bueckers, Caitlin Clark and Rhyne Howard. In one three-possession sequence, Howared found Bueckers on a backdoor baseline cut. Then Bueckers cut into the high post while Stewart was running the offense to get an uncontested midrange jumper. The Dallas Wings star followed that by diming up Angel Reese inside, and Reese was fouled for two free throws.

This is the trio’s first time representing Team USA at the senior level, but the group won a gold medal together with Aliyah Boston in 2019 at the U-19 World Cup. Their bench minutes together have demonstrated that chemistry.

Howard’s defense was critical to Team USA creating separation early. The WNBA’s steals leader had five takeaways, allowing the Americans to get out in the open floor. Howard’s major international experience has come in 3×3, but she has been a more natural fit in five-on-five, acting as a combo forward with some needed size and spacing.

Czechia never truly threatened after halftime, enabling coach Kara Lawson to play reserves for most of the final 20 minutes. Every member of Team USA scored while playing at least 10 minutes.

The Americans kept the same starting lineup through all three group games, leaning on the experience of the five rostered players who have previously won gold in a World Cup or Olympics (Stewart, Chelsea Gray, Kahleah Copper, Jackie Young and Napheesa Collier). The young reserves have started to assert themselves in pockets, and that continued against Czechia.

Bueckers was comfortable finding her spots, finishing with 10 points on 5-of-8 shooting and five assists. Team USA was a team-high plus-27 in her 19 minutes. Clark had a team-best seven assists to two turnovers and ended the game with more points than field-goal attempts even though her 3-point jumper continued to elude her.

Boston wasn’t needed as much against Czechia as she was against Italy because of the game’s faster tempo, but Reese made her mark defending on the perimeter and Kiki Iriafen was dominant on the glass, collecting 11 boards in her 14 minutes.
